title: Towards Reward Fairness in RLHF: From a Resource Allocation Perspective
findings: The paper found that the standard Bradley-Terry (BT) reward model exhibits unfairness by assigning higher rewards to more stereotypical sentences from the CrowS-Pairs dataset. In contrast, the proposed methods, Fairness Regularization (FR RM) and Fairness Coefficient (FC RM), demonstrate greater fairness by showing smaller distributional differences in rewards for stereotypical vs. non-stereotypical sentences.

measurement_description: The paper uses the CrowS-Pairs benchmark to measure social bias. Specifically, it assesses whether reward models assign higher scores to more stereotypical sentences compared to less stereotypical ones. This includes stereotypes related to various social categories, one of which is religion.
